note: The curated half of the Live Feed. YouTube tells us which video is live right now; it cannot tell us that a channel points at a harbour in Maine. That part is human, and this is where it lives. Curate CHANNELS, never videos — channel handles are permanent, video IDs are reissued every time a 24/7 stream restarts, which is exactly how the first registry died (commit edb57f6).
howToAdd: 1. Find a channel that runs a live place-cam. Copy its @handle from the URL.
2. Add an entry below with the place metadata YouTube can't give us.
3. Push. The next workflow run resolves the handle and reports whether it found anything live.
Handles that don't resolve are logged and skipped — they never break the run.

fields.handle: YouTube @handle. Preferred over channelId — readable, and stable across renames.
fields.channelId: Optional. Set it directly if you already know the UC… id; skips a lookup.
fields.maxStreams: How many simultaneous live videos to take from this channel. 1 for single-camera channels. Networks like explore.org run dozens at once — raise it and each live video becomes its own entry, titled from the video.
fields.lat/lng: Only meaningful when maxStreams is 1. Multi-camera channels get 0,0 because the coordinates differ per camera. The map (app_plan.md §3.3) needs real values; the list-only MVP does not.

channels.why: Their own YouTube channel — the sanctioned way to show their cameras. Their website forbids reproduction without written permission and serves a stripped page to non-browsers; the embed is offered deliberately and costs us nothing.
